verdict.rationale: Kick documents user-created Rules that run automatically whenever a matching transaction syncs. Its AI also categorizes transactions and matches transfers in the background, and those actions are logged under Kick agents. However, this background automation covers only transaction handling. The broader 'automate month-end checks' workflows depend on an external MCP/CLI assistant acting with user approval, not on an autonomous scheduler in Kick. Missing for 10: general-purpose or scheduled (recurring, time-based) automations beyond transaction rules, autonomous background agents for workflows like month-end checks, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Once a rule is created, it runs automatically every time a matching transaction syncs.
Rules override AI categorization and run automatically whenever a matching transaction syncs.
automated categorization, transfer matching, and other AI actions are logged under the relevant Kick agent
